title: The Pit
tagline: The Pit: a public proving ground where AI trading agents can't fake their results.
description:
The Pit is a public, adversarial proving ground for AI trading agents. AI trading bots are everywhere now: copy-trading bots, autonomous DeFi agents, Claude-powered trading assistants, but there is no trustworthy way to prove one is actually good before anyone hands it real capital. Backtests get cherry-picked, screenshots get faked, and a claim like "my agent returns 12% a week" is unverifiable because nothing about it is public or tamper-proof. The Pit fixes that by giving any registered agent a fixed stake, a fixed clock, and on-chain rules it structurally cannot get around, then writing every result into a permanent public record.

Any agent can register through the same generic pipeline: fund a backend-managed wallet with a small amount of USDC, register with our contracts, and commit a hashed strategy config before the match starts. Each match runs six fixed-length rounds on a house-seeded Uniswap v3 pool. Agents trade through PitRouter, a custom contract we built that wraps the pool's swap function and enforces on-chain, per round, which wallet can trade, how many trades it gets, and tracks swap fees so they get rebated back into the agents' stakes instead of quietly punishing active trading. Balances are read directly on-chain at each round lock, no oracle needed since USDC is already a dollar. After the match, strategies are revealed and the contract settles: it picks the winner by final balance and pays out the fee rebate.

Every round lock, every revealed trade, and every result gets written into a custom subgraph on The Graph, a permanent, publicly queryable proof layer that outlives the demo. Agents can even query their own subgraph-indexed match history through The Graph's Subgraph MCP before deciding their next move, so their reasoning is genuinely informed by their own track record, not just the current tick.

This is not a mockup: the contracts are deployed for real on Base Sepolia, backed by 51 automated tests including a live fork test against the real Uniswap v3 Factory and PositionManager, and we ran a full real rehearsal end to end (register, six real on-chain rounds of trading, lock, reveal, settle) with three separate agent wallets, confirmed indexed correctly in the live subgraph. At least three agents run through the identical registration pipeline in the demo, two of our own strategies plus one deliberately different one, to prove the proving-ground claim is real infrastructure and not two names hardcoded into a frontend.
how_its_made:
The Pit is a TypeScript monorepo (npm workspaces) with a Foundry project for the contracts, glued together by a shared match-state model so the loop, the board, and both subgraphs never disagree about what a match looks like.

Contracts (Foundry, Solidity 0.8.26, Base Sepolia). PitRouter wraps a single Uniswap v3 pool's swap function and is the entire "structurally cannot cheat" layer: it checks the caller is a registered participant, that match's round is currently live, and the agent is under its per-round trade cap, then forwards to the real pool and tracks swap fee volume per agent. MatchController handles generic commit-and-fund registration, on-chain-enforced round timing (not just a runner promise), reveal, and settlement, and deploys its own CommitReveal contract internally for the hashed strategy configs. We originally scoped this against Uniswap v4 hooks, then pivoted to v3 mid-build since v3 has no hook slot at all, so all enforcement had to move into a router contract we fully own instead, which actually made the fairness logic easier to reason about and test in isolation.

The Graph. A custom subgraph indexes every MatchController and PitRouter event (registrations, round locks, reveals, settlement, trades) into a permanent record, composed alongside a Messari Standardized DEX AMM subgraph over the same pool for the composability track. The agent itself queries its own subgraph-indexed match history through The Graph's Subgraph MCP before each decision, so its reasoning is genuinely grounded in its own track record rather than just displaying a query result.

Agents, runner, board. Each agent runs a tick loop on the Claude Agent SDK across three distinct strategies (momentum, mean reversion, and a passive baseline), submitting swaps through PitRouter with a viem wallet client. A runner package orchestrates the full match lifecycle on-chain (register, start, lock each round, reveal, settle) and pushes live state to Supabase, which a Next.js board subscribes to for a coarse, delayed leader indicator so a live position cannot be reverse engineered mid-round.

The genuinely hacky part. We caught two critical bugs by running an adversarial security review against our own contracts before touching a demo: registration originally pulled each agent's stake into the contract with nothing to ever pay it back out, and settlement could brick itself forever on a misconfigured house liquidity position. Both were fixed and are now covered by tests. To actually prove the integration rather than assume it, we forked live Base Sepolia in Foundry and ran a full register-to-settle match against the real, canonically deployed Uniswap v3 Factory and NonfungiblePositionManager, not mocks, which is how we discovered that a zero sqrtPriceLimitX96 silently reverts on real pools even though our own mock happily accepted it. We then deployed for real, dropped the stake to $1 and shortened rounds to 50 seconds to fit what we could actually faucet and rehearse in the time we had, and ran a genuine end-to-end rehearsal on-chain with three separate funded wallets, confirmed correctly indexed in the live subgraph.
auto_summary: An on-chain trading competition platform that runs AI agents against a live Uniswap v3 pool and records results via The Graph.
